summary: Walter Eugene Clark was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard, Berlin under Richard Pischel, and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He taught at the University of Chicago (1908–1927) and served as Harvard's Wales Professor of Sanskrit (1927–1950).

Walter Ewer was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Fort William College (c. 1802–1803). He served in the Bengal Civil Service as a civil servant from 1803 to 1840 and was made a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1840.

Walter Friedländer worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Berlin under Albrecht Weber, served as Professor of Art History at the University of Freiburg (1921–1933), and later was Professor of Art History at New York University (1935–1966).

Walter Kaufmann was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He studied under Franz Schreker, Curt Sachs, Gustav Becking, and Paul Nettl. He headed classical music at All India Radio (c. 1937–1946) and was Professor of Ethnomusicology at Indiana University (1957–1977).

Walter Liebenthal specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Otto Strauss, Johannes Nobel, and Max Walleser, earning his Dr. phil. at Breslau. His posts included Peking University (1937–1945), Visva-Bharati University (1952–1960), and Tübingen (1964–1982).

Walter M. Spink was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Amherst College and earning a PhD from Harvard University, he taught at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and served as a professor at the University of Michigan (c. 1961–2000).

Walter Neisser specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at the University of Breslau (c. 1878–1880) and completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen (c. 1880–1882) under the supervision of August Fick and Theodor Benfey.

Walter Nowick was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto from 1950 to 1965. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded the Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Petersen was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at Yale University in 1908. He held professorships at Bethany College (1908), the University of Florida (c. 1926–1929), and the University of Chicago (1930).

Walter Porzig was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jena, Leipzig, and Munich under Ferdinand Sommer and Ernst Windisch. His main posts included professorships at the University of Bern (1925), University of Jena (1935), University of Strasbourg (1941–1945), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1951).

Walter Ruben was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, and Sten Konow. He served as Professor of Indology at Ankara University (1935–1948), Professor of Ethnology at the University of Chile (1948–1950), and Indology professor at Humboldt University (1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, studying at Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke. He held posts at Humboldt University (1919–1935) and served as Reader and later Professor of Chinese at the University of London (1938–1960).

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1995 to 2019.

Walter Sutton Page was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Reader of Bengali at the University of Oxford and held the post of Reader of Bengali at SOAS University of London from around 1930 to 1938.

Walter William Skeat was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, Cambridge, and later held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1878 to 1912.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz was a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Stanford University, the University of Oxford, and the University of Rennes, and was a disciple of Kazi Dawa Samdup from circa 1919 to 1922.

Walther Eidlitz was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied building engineering at TU Wien from circa 1911 to 1914 and later studied under his guru, Swami Sadananda, between approximately 1941 and 1957.

Walther Heissig studied Central Asian, religious, and Tibetan studies at Vienna, Berlin, and Göttingen. He taught at Fu Jen Catholic University and Peking University in the 1940s, before serving as apl. Professor and Chair of Central Asian Studies at the University of Bonn (1957–1982).

Walther Marcus was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Giessen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Heidelberg University, where he earned his Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Christian Bartholomae between approximately 1911 and 1914.

Walther Michaelis was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1893–1898) under Albrecht Weber. He served as Director of the Francke Foundations from 1931 to 1935.
